title: Noetherian directed colimits of regular local rings are regular local
statement: Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed partially ordered set, and let $(L_i,\mathfrak m_i)_{i\in I}$ be commutative regular local rings [def-weil-regular-scheme]. For $i\leq j$ let $u_{ij}:L_i\to L_j$ be unital ring homomorphisms with $u_{ii}=\mathrm{id}$ and $u_{jk}\circ u_{ij}=u_{ik}$, and assume they are local: $u_{ij}^{-1}(\mathfrak m_j)=\mathfrak m_i$. Let $L=\varinjlim_i L_i$ be the colimit in commutative rings [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. If $L$ is Noetherian [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], then $L$ is a regular local ring. Here a local ring has a unique maximal ideal; regular local means Noetherian with maximal ideal generated by $\dim L$ elements, where dimension is Krull dimension, as in [def-weil-regular-scheme].

source.place: Tag 07DX, lemma-colimit-regular, statement at lines 25834–25838; directed system of regular local rings with local transition maps and Noetherian colimit.

proof.text: Write $v_i:L_i\to L$ for the coprojections and put $\mathfrak m=\{v_i(a):i\in I,\ a\in\mathfrak m_i\}$. The representation and equality assertions of [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise] apply because the small nonempty directed poset is filtered. To add two such elements, move their representatives to a common upper stage; both remain in that stage's maximal ideal by locality, so their sum represents an element of $\mathfrak m$. Negatives stay there as well. To multiply by any element of $L$, represent the latter at a stage and move both representatives to a common upper stage; the product is again in its maximal ideal. Thus $\mathfrak m$ is an ideal. It is proper: if $v_i(a)=1$ with $a\in\mathfrak m_i$, the equality assertion gives $k\ge i$ with $u_{ik}(a)=1$; the left side belongs to $\mathfrak m_k$, a contradiction.

source.place: Tag 07DX, lemma-colimit-regular, opening sentence; elementwise details from Tags 00D6 and 00D7.

proof.text:
Every element $b
otin\mathfrak m$ has a representative $a\in L_i$ by [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise]. Necessarily $a
otin\mathfrak m_i$, hence $a$ is a unit by [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion], and its inverse maps to an inverse of $b$. Since $\mathfrak m$ is proper, no element of it is a unit. Consequently $L/\mathfrak m$ is a nonzero field, so $\mathfrak m$ is maximal; every proper ideal is contained in $\mathfrak m$, since an element outside it is a unit. Therefore $L$ is a nonzero local ring with unique maximal ideal $\mathfrak m$. Moreover $v_i^{-1}(\mathfrak m)=\mathfrak m_i$: one inclusion is by construction; for the reverse, $a
otin\mathfrak m_i$ is a unit, whose image cannot belong to the proper ideal $\mathfrak m$. In particular each coprojection is local.

source.place: Tag 07DX, lemma-colimit-regular, opening sentence expanded; Tag 00E9, lemma-characterize-local-ring.

proof.text: By [lem-sc-regular-local-domain], every $L_i$ is a domain. If $ab=0$ in $L$, represent $a,b$ at a common stage $i$ using [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise], say by $a_i,b_i$. Its equality assertion, applied to the image of $a_i b_i$ and zero, gives $j\ge i$ with $u_{ij}(a_i)u_{ij}(b_i)=0$. The domain $L_j$ forces one factor to be zero, hence $a=0$ or $b=0$. Together with $1\ne0$ from step 2 this proves that $L$ is a domain. This argument does not require injective transition maps.

source.place: Tag 07DX, lemma-colimit-regular, penultimate sentence; domain input is Tag 00NP, lemma-regular-domain (deduced there from 00NO).

proof.text: For all diagrams in the statement simultaneously, prove the result by strong induction on the least number $n$ of generators of the maximal ideal of their Noetherian colimit. This number exists by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Steps 1--3 apply to every such diagram, independently of the induction. If $n=0$, then $\mathfrak m=0$ and step 2 makes $L$ a field. Its only prime ideal is zero, so $\dim L=0$ and it is regular by [def-weil-regular-scheme]. Suppose $n>0$ and assume the assertion for all diagrams whose colimit maximal ideal needs fewer than $n$ generators. Choose generators $x,x_2,\ldots,x_n$ of $\mathfrak m$ of minimal cardinality. Then $x\notin\mathfrak m^2$: otherwise the images of $x_2,\ldots,x_n$ span $\mathfrak m/\mathfrak m^2$ and [lem-weil-pbc-nakayama-local-generators], with the finitely generated $L$-module $M=\mathfrak m$, says that these $n-1$ elements generate $\mathfrak m$, contrary to minimality. In particular $x\ne0$.

source.place: Tag 07DX, lemma-colimit-regular, induction and choice of x; minimal-generator formulation of its cotangent-dimension induction, using Tag 00DV, lemma-NAK (4), (8).

proof.text: Represent $x$ by $x_i\in L_i$ using [lem-pc-filtered-colimit-commrings-elementwise]. Step 2 gives $x_i\in\mathfrak m_i$. For $j\ge i$ put $x_j=u_{ij}(x_i)$. These belong to $\mathfrak m_j$ and not to $\mathfrak m_j^2$: membership in that square would express $x_j$ as a finite sum of products of elements of $\mathfrak m_j$, whose image would express $x$ as an element of $\mathfrak m^2$, contradicting step 4. Thus [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-hypersurface-criterion] gives regular local rings $Q_j=L_j/x_jL_j$ for every $j\ge i$. The transition maps descend to $Q_j\to Q_k$ because $u_{jk}(x_j)=x_k$.

source.place: Tag 07DX, lemma-colimit-regular, choice of x_i and application of Tag 00NQ, lemma-regular-ring-CM, with c=1.

proof.text: The tail $I_{\ge i}$ is small, nonempty and directed. It still has colimit $L$: extend any compatible ring cocone $f_j:L_j\to T$ on the tail to an arbitrary index $h$ by $f_k u_{hk}$ for a common upper bound $k\ge h,i$. Two choices agree after passing to an upper bound of both, and the extension is compatible. The universal property [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit] for $L$ now gives existence and uniqueness of the induced map. For a ring $T$, compatible maps $Q_j\to T$ are exactly compatible maps $L_j\to T$ on this tail which kill $x_j$. Their unique map $L\to T$ kills $x$, and hence factors uniquely through $L/xL$. Conversely a map $L/xL\to T$ gives these maps $Q_j\to T$. Thus the natural quotient cocone exhibits $\overline L=L/xL$ as the colimit of the $Q_j$ in commutative rings. This is a direct verification of the universal property, not an assumption that arbitrary colimits preserve underlying sets.

source.place: Tag 07DX, lemma-colimit-regular, displayed identification of the quotient colimit; Categories Tag 002F, definition-colimit, used directly.

proof.text: The quotient $\overline L$ is local with maximal ideal $\overline{\mathfrak m}=\mathfrak m/xL$: this ideal is proper and every element outside it is the image of a unit of $L$ (step 2). Likewise the maximal ideal of $Q_j$ is $\mathfrak m_j/x_jL_j$; the same quotient argument applies to $L_j$ using [lem-weil-pbc-local-ring-unit-criterion]. For $j\le k$ in the tail, a class represented by $a\in L_j$ maps into the maximal ideal of $Q_k$ if and only if $u_{jk}(a)\in\mathfrak m_k$, if and only if $a\in\mathfrak m_j$. Thus every quotient transition map is local. The quotient $\overline L$ is Noetherian by [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]: the inverse image of any ideal is a finitely generated ideal of $L$, whose generator images generate the given ideal. Finally $\overline{\mathfrak m}$ is generated by the images of $x_2,\ldots,x_n$, since the image of $x$ is zero. Its least number of generators is therefore at most $n-1$. The diagram of $Q_j$ now meets every hypothesis of the strong induction hypothesis from step 4, so $\overline L$ is regular local.

source.place: Tag 07DX, lemma-colimit-regular, application of induction to the Noetherian quotient; quotient locality and generator count expanded from the definitions.

proof.text: Step 3 and $x\ne0$ show that $x$ is a nonzerodivisor of $L$. The hypotheses of [lem-weil-pbc-dimension-quotient-nonzerodivisor] hold: $L$ is Noetherian and local, and $x\in\mathfrak m$. Hence $\dim L=\dim\overline L+1$. Since $\overline L$ is regular, [def-weil-regular-scheme] supplies generators of its maximal ideal numbering $\dim\overline L$. Lift them to $y_1,\ldots,y_r\in\mathfrak m$, where $r=\dim\overline L$. For $a\in\mathfrak m$, express its quotient class as $\sum\overline c_t\overline y_t$ and lift the coefficients. The difference $a-\sum c_t y_t$ lies in $xL$. Thus $x,y_1,\ldots,y_r$ generate $\mathfrak m$ and number $\dim L$. The Noetherian local ring $L$ is regular by that definition. This completes the induction and the proof.
